author: Altschuler, Eric Lewin
title: Bachanalia: The Essential Listener's Guide to Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier
annotation: Informal guide introducing Bach's contrapuntal art to readers without formal musical training; its analysis is limited to listing subject entries.

author: Badura-Skoda, Paul
title: Interpreting Bach at the Keyboard (trans. Alfred Clayton; orig. Bach-Interpretation: Die Klavierwerke Johann Sebastian Bachs, Laaber, 1990)
annotation: Monograph on performance of Bach's keyboard works.

author: Boekelman, Bernardus
title: Acht Fugen aus J. S. Bach's Wohltemperirtem Clavier durch Farben analytisch dargestellt ... Serie I [and II]
annotation: Colour-coded piano-score analyses of sixteen fugues (I.1-7, 10, 16, 21, 22; II.1, 2, 7, 11, 12) separating thematic from non-thematic material; not always thorough.

author: Brandts Buys, Hans
title: Het Wohltemperirte Clavier van Johann Sebastian Bach
annotation: Commentary on every movement of the 48, preceded by short discussions of fugal technique and historical issues (reissued 1955, 1984).

author: Bruhn, Siglind
title: J. S. Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier: In-Depth Analysis and Interpretation (4 vols.)
annotation: Methodical, systematic movement-by-movement discussion aimed at advanced performers; Tomita finds it covers the trivial at the expense of the important, and her refusal to separate answers from subjects and codettas from episodes unhelpful for analysis, though her colour diagrams are user-friendly.

author: Bruyck, Carl van
title: Technische und ästhetische Analysen des Wohltemperirten Claviers ...
annotation: One of the earliest monographs on the 48; discussions often too brief, some observations aesthetic and not well conceived.

author: Bullivant, Roger
title: Fugue
annotation: Called probably the most insightful monograph: treats fugue historically and analytically, clearing up confusions between academic fugue and real composition, with many examples from the 48.

author: Busoni, Ferruccio (ed., with Egon Petri and Bruno Mugellini)
title: Johann Sebastian Bach: Klavierwerke
annotation: Practical edition full of dynamic marks; some fugues carry analytical indications.

author: Czaczkes, Ludwig
title: Analyse des Wohltemperierten Klaviers. Form und Aufbau der Fuge bei Bach (2 vols.; i: 1956, ii: 1965)
annotation: Very detailed formal analysis of all movements, long regarded as the classic textbook; sometimes over-indulgent and speculative.

author: Czaczkes, Ludwig
title: Die Fugen des Wohltemperierten Klaviers in bildlicher Darstellung
annotation: Detailed analytical diagrams of all the fugues, based on his earlier book.

author: David, Johann Nepomuk
title: Das Wohltemperierte Klavier. Der Versuch einer Synopsis
annotation: Brief, speculative analysis trying to derive motives/subjects from one another and to relate pieces in the same key thematically.

author: Dehn, Siegfried Wilhelm
title: Analysen dreier Fugen aus Joh. Seb. Bach's wohltemperiertem Klavier und einer Vocal-Doppelfuge A. M. Bononcini's
annotation: Detailed, nearly bar-by-bar motivic (and limited harmonic) analysis of I.6, II.7 and II.9.

author: Dickinson, Alan Edgar Frederic
title: Bach's Fugal Works. With an Account of Fugue before and after Bach
annotation: Brief commentary on the main stylistic and structural traits of many fugues, by Bach (48 and organ) and other composers.

author: Dürr, Alfred
title: Johann Sebastian Bach. Das Wohltemperierte Klavier
annotation: Groundbreaking monograph by the NBA editor, combining historical and analytical issues with source variants and evaluating other scholars' views; like other Germans, summarises each fugue in two levels (sections and expositions).

author: Fuller-Maitland, John Alexander
title: The "48": Bach's Wohltemperirtes Clavier (2 vols.)
publisher_or_journal: London: Humphrey Milford / Oxford University Press
annotation: Very brief commentary on each movement.

author: Gedalge, André
title: Treatise on the Fugue (trans. and ed. Ferdinand Davis; orig. Traité de la fugue, 1900)
annotation: Well laid-out student textbook; uses examples from the 48 for answer (I.18), episodes (II.22) and stretto (I.1, 4; II.5, 9, 22, 23).

author: Gray, Cecil William Turpie
title: The Forty-eight Preludes and Fugues of J. S. Bach
annotation: Concise analytical commentary focused on style and effect of each movement.

author: Higgs, James
title: Fugue
annotation: Concise textbook for students learning to write fugues.

author: Horsley, Imogene
title: Fugue: History and Practice
publisher_or_journal: New York: Free Press; London: Collier-Macmillan
annotation: Textbook on the history and writing of fugue; some 48 examples, but rather basic.

author: Iliffe, Frederick
title: The Forty-eight Preludes and Fugues of John Sebastian Bach Analysed for the Use of Students
annotation: Very brief outline analysis/description of each movement; leaves Bach's compositional detail mostly untouched.

author: Jadassohn, Salomon
title: Erläuterungen zu ausgewählten Fugen aus Johann Sebastian Bach's wohltemperirtem Clavier (supplement to his Lehrbuch des Kanons und der Fuge)
annotation: Fairly detailed structural analysis of nineteen fugues (I.1, 4, 6, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 22, 23, 24; II.2, 5, 7, 9, 10, 22, 23).

author: Jones, Richard (ed.); commentary by Donald Francis Tovey
title: J. S. Bach: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Part I [and II]
publisher_or_journal: London: Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music
annotation: Well-researched critical edition with excellent commentary on genesis, sources and editorial issues; reprints Tovey's 1924 commentary, lightly revised.

author: Keller, Hermann
title: The Well-Tempered Clavier by Johann Sebastian Bach (trans. Leigh Gerdine; orig. Das Wohltemperierte Klavier, Kassel, 1965)
annotation: Captures the emotional content well; interpretations often unique and controversial, analysis mostly limited to subject and salient features, lacking detail for serious study.

author: Kennan, Kent Wheeler
title: Counterpoint Based on Eighteenth-Century Practice (2nd ed.)
annotation: Basic counterpoint textbook leading to fugue writing, with many examples from the 48.

author: Kirkpatrick, Ralph
title: Interpreting Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier: A Performer's Discourse of Method
publisher_or_journal: New Haven and London: Yale University Press
annotation: Performer who dismisses conventional analysis as 'autopsy'; draws on history, theory and aesthetics to show how to interpret the 48 with conviction.

author: Kirnberger, Johann Philipp
title: Die Kunst des reinen Satzes in der Musik (2 vols.)
annotation: Magnum opus on music theory; six examples from the 48 (I.1, 4; II.4, 10, 11, 22) on metre, rhythm, harmony and counterpoint.

author: Kirnberger, Johann Philipp
title: Die wahren Grundsätze zum Gebrauch der Harmonie
annotation: Includes figured-bass harmonic analyses of I.24 and II.Pr.20 (by his pupil J. A. P. Schulz); repr. Bach-Dokumente III no. 781; Eng. trans. Beach and Thym, JMT 23 (1979). Serwer's article on the Marpurg-Kirnberger controversy is also cited.

author: Kitson, Charles Herbert
title: Studies in Fugue
annotation: Fugue-writing textbook stressing good countersubjects and episodes; 48 examples of little analytical value.

author: Kitson, Charles Herbert
title: Elements of Fugal Construction
annotation: Concise student textbook; through 48 examples it occasionally discusses pitfalls of certain fugal devices.

author: Knorr, Iwan Otto Armand
title: Die Fugen des "Wohltemperierten Klaviers" von Joh. Seb. Bach in bildlicher Darstellung
annotation: Very brief, rough diagram analysis of all the fugues, merely marking subject entries.

author: Macpherson, Stewart
title: A Commentary on Book I [and Book II] of the Forty-Eight Preludes and Fugues of Johann Sebastian Bach
annotation: Commentary on each movement focusing on key structural features; probably the most useful of the books of its period for students.

author: Marpurg, Friedrich Wilhelm
title: Abhandlung von der Fuge (2 vols.)
annotation: First substantial (conservative) discussion of Bach's fugal art; sixteen examples from the 48 (I.1, 8, 10, 18, 20, 24; II.1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 11, 13, 16, 21, 22); partial English translation in Mann, The Study of Fugue (1958).

author: Morgan, Orlando
title: J. S. Bach: Forty-eight Preludes and Fugues. Analysis of the Fugues
annotation: Very concise constructional discussion of all the fugues, largely based on Prout but expanding where he disagrees with his teacher.

author: Nalden, Charles
title: Fugal Answer
publisher_or_journal: London: Auckland University Press / Oxford University Press
annotation: Comprehensive theoretical and historical study of the fugal answer, critically examining other scholars' theories.

author: Oldroyd, George
title: The Technique and Spirit of Fugue: An Historical Study
annotation: Systematic study of fugal technique and style treating the 48 as 'an embodiment of truth'; many examples, but analysis too limited and fragmented.

author: Perrachio, Luigi
title: G. S. Bach: Il Clavicembalo ben temperato
annotation: Analytical commentary on each movement (an expanded 1947 Turin edition was not consulted).

author: Potgieter, Zelda
title: Analyses of Selected Works from the Well-Tempered Clavier of J. S. Bach: A Synthesis of Existing Approaches (D.Phil. diss., 2 vols.)
publisher_or_journal: University of Port Elizabeth, South Africa
annotation: Weighs strengths and weaknesses of various analytical approaches and proposes a multifaceted model, using II.16 as example.

author: Prout, Ebenezer
title: Fugue
annotation: Classic fugue textbook with ample 48 examples (21 fugues from Book I, 12 from Book II).

author: Prout, Ebenezer
title: Fugal Analysis: A Companion to "Fugue"
annotation: Collection of fugues in score with analyses, mainly Bach; II.20 is the only fugue from the 48 discussed.

author: Prout, Ebenezer
title: Analysis of J. S. Bach's Forty-Eight Fugues (Das Wohltemperirte Clavier), ed. Louis B. Prout
annotation: Posthumous concise constructional discussion of all 48 fugues.

author: Renwick, William
title: Analyzing Fugue: A Schenkerian Approach
annotation: Thorough Schenkerian analysis of nearly 300 fugues by Bach and contemporaries; many, often insightful, 48 examples.

author: Riemann, Hugo
title: Analysis of J. S. Bach's Wohltemperirtes Clavier (trans. J. S. Shedlock; 2 vols.; orig. Analyse von Bachs wohltemperirtem Klavier, 1890)
annotation: Serious, original analysis of all movements, critical of earlier writers (esp. Bruyck); hard to follow owing to poor translation and pedantic, unreferenced discussion.

author: Sampson, Brook
title: A Digest of the Analysis of J. S. Bach's Forty-eight Celebrated Fugues from the Well-Tempered Clavier
annotation: Very systematic constructional analysis, but poorly presented and with many errors in text and examples.

author: Sampson, Brook
title: Outline Analysis of Each of Bach's Forty-Eight Fugues
annotation: Shorter version of the Digest, showing only construction and keys of entries.

author: Schulenberg, David
title: The Keyboard Music of J. S. Bach
annotation: Broad discussion of all Bach's keyboard music; on the 48 it is coloured by source study and style analysis, a refreshing approach for performers.

author: Souchay, Marc-André
title: Das Thema in der Fuge Bachs
annotation: First of two parts on Bach's fugues, dealing with fugue subjects, their types and construction, with many 48 examples.

author: Stade, Fritz
title: J. S. Bach. Die Fugen des wohltemperierten Klaviers partiturmässig dargestellt und nach ihrem Bau erläutert (2 vols.)
annotation: All the fugues in open score with detailed remarks highlighting themes, motives and their variants.

author: Taylor, Franklin
title: Treatise on Canon and Fugue (trans. and adapted from E. F. Richter, Lehrbuch der Fuge, 1859)
annotation: Practical fugue-writing guide, with the translator revising much (esp. harmonic analysis); many 48 examples but not very critical.

author: Tovey, Donald Francis
title: "Commentary" in J. S. Bach: Forty-Eight Preludes and Fugues (ed. Tovey, fingered by Harold Samuel), Books I and II
publisher_or_journal: London: Associated Board of the R.A.M. and R.C.M.
annotation: Classic reading for advanced performers: succinct analytical points and advice on stylish performance; reproduced and corrected in Jones's 1994 edition.
